title: Nirvana: Not The Band
summary: Josh and Chuck explore Nirvana, the Buddhist concept of liberation from suffering and the cycle of rebirth, framed as the third or fourth part of a loose enlightenment series after the Karma and Reincarnation episodes. They cover Siddhartha Gautama's privileged youth, his encounters with an old man, a sick man and a corpse, his ascetic period, his enlightenment under the tree, the Four Noble Truths and Noble Eightfold Path, and how Buddhist nirvana compares with Hindu moksha, including karma, the varna caste system, Gandhi's expulsion from his caste, and the four Hindu aims (dharma, artha, kama, moksha). A listener mail segment covers German sabotage in World War One, including the Black Tom explosion.

segments.title: Opening banter and enlightenment series
segments.summary: Hosts banter and agree to make Nirvana the third or fourth part of an enlightenment series after the Karma and Reincarnation episodes, mention friend Rachel Grundy's Buddhism, and joke about Hinduism and Buddhism as spinoffs.

segments.title: Siddhartha's early life and window revelation
segments.summary: Siddhartha Gautama is introduced as a sheltered, wealthy prince from a ruling warrior class who grows dissatisfied after seeing an old man, a sick man and a corpse from his palace window, and then leaves his family to seek enlightenment.

segments.title: Ascetic hardship, the middle way and enlightenment
segments.summary: Siddhartha tries extreme poverty and starvation, decides this is not the path, accepts a meal from a stranger, and sits under a tree where he reaches enlightenment and nirvana, which literally means extinguishing suffering, hatred and ignorance.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Short ad break in the middle of the Buddhism discussion.

segments.title: Karma, samsara and attaining nirvana
segments.summary: Karma is explained as a reward or consequence for past actions, likened to Newton's third law; nirvana stops the accrual of bad karma, and parinirvana is the final state after death, outside the cycle of samsara.

segments.title: Nirvana Day, buddhas and arhats
segments.summary: Nirvana Day is celebrated February 15 in East Asia. A Buddha is distinguished from the Buddha, and an arhat is a enlightened person who is not omniscient. The Buddha taught for the last forty-five years of his life.

segments.title: Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path
segments.summary: The Four Noble Truths are life is suffering, suffering is caused by ignorance, suffering ends by overcoming craving, and the Noble Eightfold Path leads there. The eight paths are grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and concentration divisions.

segments.title: Hindu moksha, varna caste system and Gandhi
segments.summary: Hindu moksha is compared with Buddhist nirvana, with reincarnation through castes and species, the deities Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, and Gandhi's expulsion from his merchant caste for championing the lowest caste. The hosts discuss whether the caste system still fits modern Hinduism.

segments.title: Four Hindu aims: dharma, artha, kama and moksha
segments.summary: The four aims of Hinduism are described: dharma as duty to one's caste and calling, artha as pursuit of wealth, kama as desire, and moksha as liberation.

segments.title: Listener mail: German sabotage in World War One
segments.summary: A listener from Uganda writes about the German sabotage ring run from New York during World War One under Kaiser Wilhelm II, including the Black Tom Island munitions depot explosion in 1914 that damaged the Statue of Liberty, and failed plots involving bombs and passport fraud.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and point to social media, email and the website for more episodes.
